newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Trading quiet after Dow sell-off.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Trading quiet after Dow sell-off.

text.p: Trading was light after the U.S. market close on Monday, despite a sell-off during regular hours trading that knocked 192 points off the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Dealers reported that neither Computer Sciences Corp nor BankBoston traded after hours.
Computer Sciences said after the close of trade that it anticipated a $0.02 share gain during its fiscal first quarter.
BankBoston announced late in the day that it expected to see proceeds of $340 million from the sale of its consumer finance unit to Norwest Corp.
"It's kind of drifted down towards the end of the day," a dealer said of trading momentum after the bell.

The after-hours calm followed a rocky day for the Dow industrials, which plunged 192 points, or 2.47 percent, to an unofficial close of 7604 in regular hours trading. The slide was the second largest in point terms in the average's history, although in percentage terms it did not rank near the top 10 declines.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume rose to 250,600, compared with 64,500 from Friday. Session two volume hit 5,359,555, up from Friday's 308,300.
